question: Which of the following is equal to the value of 1 Volt? (assume J-joule, C-coulomb, s-second)
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 J/C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **1 Volt** is defined as the difference in electric potential between two points when 1 joule of energy is used to move 1 coulomb of charge between those points.
 
• The unit of voltage, the **volt (V)**, is equivalent to 1 joule per coulomb (J/C).
 
• In the International System of Units (SI), voltage is a derived unit expressed in **joules per coulomb**.
 
• This definition is consistent with the equation V=(W)/(Q), where V is voltage, W is work (in joules), and Q is charge (in coulombs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:** Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, given by the formula V=IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• **Electric Potential:** Electric potential is the amount of electric potential energy per unit charge at a certain position in an electric field.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** Voltage is a measure of the energy conversion per unit charge, which is vital in understanding how electrical energy is converted to other forms of energy in circuits.
 
• **Coulomb:** The coulomb (C) is the unit of electric charge in the International System of Units (SI), and it represents the quantity of electricity transported in one second by a current of one ampere.
 
• **Joule:** The joule (J) is the SI unit of work or energy, defined as the amount of work done when a force of one newton displaces a mass over one meter.
